name: Shema
overview: Shema was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Hebron. His mention in the genealogical records situates him within the lineage of Judah, underscoring his place in the biblical heritage. No additional personal notes are recorded beyond his tribal and familial connections.
namesAndTitles: The name Shema is a proper name meaning 'he hears.' This meaning reflects a common Hebrew root related to hearing and obedience, though the name was not given by God. The biblical record simply preserves this name as it appears in the genealogical context.
familyAndRelationships: Shema is recorded as the son of Hebron, linking him directly to this ancestor within the tribe of Judah. He is also noted as the father of Korah, establishing a clear father-son relationship. Additionally, Raham is identified as Shema's father, further clarifying his immediate lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Shema's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical framework of Judah, connecting important familial lines. His identification as the son of Hebron and father of Korah places him within the ancestral history that leads to later biblical figures. While no distinct narrative actions are attributed to him, his inclusion preserves the continuity of God's chosen people as recorded in Scripture.
